title: Count by tray
goal: Group the B09 jars by tray and count the jars on each tray. Then work out each tray's rate: jars with springtails out of all its jars. This editor starts each Run fresh, so build what you need again in each task. On your laptop, Julia keeps a name until you close it.
story: The report says T-C has 0 jars with springtails. What does the notebook say for each tray? Same idea as Lesson 2, new name: practice_jars is now jars, the six B09 jars.

dictionary.means: the six B09 jars of the case notebook (made up for this game), with the columns jar_id, batch_id, tray_id and detected. Julia's word: a DataFrame.
splits the jars into one group for each value of detected, true or false, and counts each group. A colon in front names a column. Julia's word: groupby and combine.
The = gives the answer a name. This editor starts each Run fresh, so name it again in the same Run. On your laptop, Julia keeps a name until you close it. Julia's word: assigning a variable.

challenges.prompt: Use groupby to put the B09 jars into groups, one group for each tray. The table jars holds the six B09 jars.
hints: Name the table first, then the column to group by: the one that says which tray a jar is on.

feedback.pass: One group per tray, and no jar lost.

errors.say: A column name needs a colon in front, like :tray_id.
In Julia the function is groupby, with no underscore.
Check the spelling. The function is groupby and the table is jars.
The four columns of jars are jar_id, batch_id, tray_id and detected. Check the column name.
groupby needs two things: the table, a comma, then the column to group by.

rounds.title: Count jars and jars with springtails

challenges.prompt: Show one row per tray with three columns: tray_id, n (jars on the tray) and detected_n (jars with springtails). Give the table the name counts.
hints: Inside combine each group gets one row. Count its rows with nrow and add up its detected values with sum.

feedback.pass: One row per tray, with both counts.

errors.say: A new column name needs a colon in front, like :detected_n.
A new column name needs a colon in front, like :n.
Check the spelling. The table is jars, and the functions are combine, groupby, nrow and sum.
nrow is a function, so it has no colon in front. Write nrow => :n.
The four columns of jars are jar_id, batch_id, tray_id and detected. Check the column name.
A pair reads :column => function => :new_name, with no brackets after the function.
Write nrow with no brackets after it: nrow => :n.
Give each new column its own name: :n for the jars on the tray, :detected_n for the jars with springtails.

challenges.prompt: This editor starts each Run fresh, so build the counts table again in this task. Then add a column rate: detected_n divided by n, a number from 0 to 1 for each tray. Show counts.
challenges.solution:
counts = combine(groupby(jars, :tray_id), nrow => :n, :detected => sum => :detected_n)
counts.rate = counts.detected_n ./ counts.n
counts
hints: Divide one column by the other with ./ (with the dot), so each tray is divided by its own n.

feedback.pass: Each tray now has its rate. Julia prints 1.0 when every jar on a tray had springtails.

close.finding: Every tray has springtails. T-A and T-B have a rate of 1.0 (every jar). T-C has 0.5: one jar of two. The report's 0 for T-C does not match the notebook.
